page: Microsoft Azure L2s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The compute allocation consists of 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. For local low-latency requirements, the system includes 480 GB of attached NVMe SSD storage. The CPU features extensive instruction set extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX matrix accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes highlight strong single-threaded performance contrasted by aggregate multi-threaded limits typical of a dual-vCPU footprint. The instance achieved a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2138.0 and gzip single-threaded compression throughput of 31.24 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics reveal throughput bottlenecks, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 2622.0 and stress-ng multi-core CPU performance in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth for large blocks recorded 20.23 GB/sec read and 14.38 GB/sec write.

Cost efficiency is centered around the inclusion of direct NVMe storage and modern single-thread processing speed. However, total compute density is limited by the single physical core. Workloads reliant on high parallel throughput or massive memory bandwidth will face constraints. Microsoft Azure L2s_v4 is appropriate for lightweight database operations, caching nodes, log aggregation, and single-threaded tasks requiring direct NVMe storage scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure L2s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs spanning a single physical core. The instance provides 16.0 GB of system memory (8.0 GB per core) and includes 480 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Single-threaded performance is high, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 2138.0 and gzip compression reaching 31.24 GB/sec. In contrast, multi-threaded tasks and uncached memory bandwidth fall into lower percentile bands due to the core count. With integrated high-speed local disk, this instance is suited for localized storage-bound tasks, small caching layers, and lightweight database engines.
